payload.name: superior-pharyngeal-constrictor
payload.scope: People made the superior-pharyngeal-constrictor construct to map the uppermost pharyngeal constrictor muscle band that forms the posterior and lateral walls of the superior pharynx, enabling clinicians to localize pharyngeal constriction defects and retropharyngeal abscesses.

definition.body: The superior pharyngeal constrictor is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the quadrate sheet of muscle forming the uppermost band of the posterior and lateral walls of the pharynx. Parameters: (1) the origins - pterygoid hamulus, pterygomandibular raphe (shared with the buccinator), and the medial pterygoid plate of the sphenoid bone; (2) the insertion - the pharyngeal tubercle of the occipital bone and the pharyngeal raphe, a midline tendon where the fibers of both sides interdigitate; (3) the fiber orientation - lower fibers run inferiorly, upper fibers overlap the middle constrictor; (4) the aperture - the stylopharyngeus nerve passes through between the superior and middle bands; (5) the clinical significance - landmark for pharyngeal surgery, origin of superior constrictor palsy in stroke, and site of pharyngoplasty for velopharyngeal insufficiency. It persists as a standard anatomical structure in human anatomy texts, otolaryngology references, and swallowing assessment protocols. e.g.: the superior pharyngeal constrictor in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition by Drake; the pharyngeal raphe during constrictor repair in Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition; stylopharyngeus nerve passing through the constrictor in Moore Clinically Oriented Anatomy, 9th edition | not: the middle-pharyngeal-constrictor (the intermediate band arising from the hyoid bone, a distinct muscle layer); the inferior-pharyngeal-constrictor arising from the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, a distinct muscle layer; the buccinator (the facial muscle sharing the pterygomandibular raphe, not a pharyngeal muscle) [formal: constrictor pharyngis superior | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]

definition.body: The middle pharyngeal constrictor is a human-authored anatomical construct that maps the fan-shaped sheet of muscle forming the intermediate band of the posterior and lateral walls of the pharynx. Parameters: (1) the origins - the lesser and greater horns of the hyoid bone and the hyoidothyroid ligament; (2) the insertion - the pharyngeal raphe and overlapping fibers posteriorly where it fuses with the superior constrictor above and the inferior constrictor below; (3) the fiber arrangement - fibers fan superiorly to overlap the superior constrictor and inferiorly to be overlapped by the inferior constrictor; (4) the aperture - the stylopharyngeus muscle passes between the superior and middle constrictors, and the glossopharyngeal nerve and tonsillar artery pass between the middle and inferior constrictors; (5) the clinical significance - landmark in tonsillectomy (the constrictor is the bed from which the tonsil is dissected), site of pharyngeal diverticula, and reference for pharyngeal pacing. Parameters: (1) the origin — apex of the styloid process and its associated stylohyoid ligament; (2) the course — descends along the lateral pharyngeal wall, passing between the superior and middle constrictor muscles to insert into the posterior border of the thyroid cartilage; (3) the innervation — glossopharyngeal nerve (CN IX), the only pharyngeal muscle with this innervation; (4) the action — elevates the pharynx and larynx during swallowing and speech, widens the pharyngeal cavity; (5) the clinical significance — landmark in tonsillectomy surgery, its atrophy assessed in glossopharyngeal nerve palsy, and its course relevant to transstyloid surgical approaches to the parapharyngeal space. payload.name: palatopharyngeus-muscle
payload.scope: People made the palatopharyngeus muscle construct to map the longitudinal pharyngeal muscle that elevates the pharynx from the soft palate origin so that clinicians can assess swallowing function, evaluate velopharyngeal disorders, and plan palatal surgery.

definition.body: The palatopharyngeus muscle is a human-authored anatomical construct mapping the paired longitudinal muscle of the pharynx originating from the soft palate, whose fibers descend to merge with the salpingopharyngeus and insert into the posterior border of the thyroid cartilage, elevating the pharynx and larynx during swallowing and forming the posterior tonsillar pillar. Parameters: (1) the origin — the palatopharyngeal aponeurosis from the posterior border of the soft palate (palatine aponeurosis); (2) the course — descends along the lateral pharyngeal wall as a muscular band; (3) the fusion — merges with the salpingopharyngeus muscle superiorly; (4) the insertion — posterior border of the thyroid cartilage and the pharyngeal wall; (5) the clinical significance — forms the palatopharyngeal fold (posterior tonsillar pillar) visible on oropharyngeal inspection, its function impaired in velopharyngeal insufficiency. It persists as a maintained anatomical landmark in head-and-neck anatomy, otolaryngology, and swallowing assessment. e.g.: palatopharyngeus described in Gray's Anatomy, 42nd edition as part of the palatopharyngeal complex; palatopharyngeal fold visualized on oral examination as the posterior tonsillar pillar; palatopharyngeus weakness assessed in velopharyngeal dysfunction per Cummings Otolaryngology, 6th edition | not: the salpingopharyngeus-muscle (the superior muscle that blends with it, originating from the auditory tube); the levator-veli-palatini (a separate soft palate muscle originating from the temporal bone, innervated differently); the tensor-veli-palatini (another soft palate muscle not part of the longitudinal pharyngeal muscle group) [formal: musculus palatopharyngeus | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes]
